newsitem.title: UK: Norwegian grades trade firmer on N.Sea wet market.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian grades trade firmer on N.Sea wet market.

text.p: North Sea spot crude showed signs of revival on Wednesday when Norwegian grades traded at firmer differentials, lending a firmer tone after a Dated Brent changed hands early at a weaker price.

Ekofisk loading April 7-9 was done at Dated Brent +15 cents, while another loading April 9-11 traded at an eight cent premium to the international benchmark. The grade traded at a five cent discount to Dated on Tuesday.
A Gullfaks C loading April 1-3 changed hands at a 10 cent premium to Dated, two cents higher than the level agreed on Tuesday for a March 29-31 loader.
An Oseberg loading April 3-5 was done at a 10 cent premium to Dated, sharply higher from discounts of two and 10 cents on Tuesday.

"The market shows potential for a gradual improvement -- although nothing spectacular -- as we move into April. There's buying out there, although the low numbers have hidden it well up to now," a trader said.
The latest trades followed the sale of a wet Brent loading March 26-28 at April Brent -90 cents in the morning, a shade lower than Tuesday's May-related deals.

The sale seemed to confirm weakness created by an oversupplied Atlantic Basin, traders said, but they cautioned that attention was focussed on the intentions of one European major holding four April Brents.
North Sea crude paper was talked at around unchanged levels in lacklustre activity. CFDs were around May -39 cents for next week, with the week after at around -30 cents.
Intermonths were steady at around +17/+22 cents for April/May.
